    AI Overview
    Duke University is a private research university located in Durham, North Carolina. Situated in the state's "Triangle" region, the campus covers nearly 9,000 acres, featuring major facilities like the main campus and the Duke Forest. It was established in its current location in 1924. 
    Key Details About Location: 
    • City: Durham, North Carolina.
    • Region: Known as the "Triangle" region, which includes Raleigh and Chapel Hill.
    • Campus Size: Approximately 8,600 to 9,000 acres, including specialized areas like a marine lab in Beaufort, N.C..
    • International Presence: Includes Duke Kunshan University in China and Duke-NUS Medical School in Singapore.

    People also ask
    What is the GPA to get into Duke?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    Duke University does not have a strict minimum GPA for admission, but it is extremely competitive, with successful applicants often holding weighted GPAs of
    4.2 or higher. A top-tier GPA is crucial for admission, but Duke uses a holistic process, weighing extracurriculars, course rigor, and letters of recommendation equally. 
    Undergraduate Admissions Requirements 
    • GPA: A competitive, largely weighted, GPA of 4.2+ is typical. Most applicants boast a 4.0 or a 3.9 unweighted GPA.
    • Transcript: Rigor of high school curriculum is highly evaluated.
    • Holistic Review: Strong extracurriculars, leadership, and personal essays are essential, as a high GPA alone is rarely enough for admission
      .
       
    Transfer and Special Programs 
    • Transfer: Competitive applicants usually hold a minimum college GPA of 3.7.
    • Pre-Health/Med: Applicants often have a cumulative and science GPA of 3.4 or higher. 
    What to Include in Your GPA Calculation 
    • All high school or college-level coursework completed.
    • Grades from all previously attended institutions.
    • All grades for repeated courses. 
    Important Considerations 
    • If your GPA is lower, you must compensate with higher SAT (typically 1470+) or ACT scores and stronger extracurricular accomplishments.
    • Duke uses a holistic evaluation, meaning no single factor—including GPA—will automatically qualify or disqualify a student.
